subject: english-literature
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: In Macbeth, which title does Macbeth already hold at the very start of the play, before any prophecy is fulfilled?
questions.explain: Macbeth begins the play as Thane of Glamis, his inherited title, before the witches greet him as Cawdor and king.

questions.q: What is identified as Macbeth's central tragic flaw that drives the plot?
questions.explain: His "vaulting ambition" leads him to murder and tyranny, the engine of his downfall.

questions.q: What apparition warns Macbeth he is safe until Birnam Wood comes to Dunsinane?
options: A crowned child holding a tree
questions.explain: The third apparition, a crowned child with a tree, promises safety until Birnam Wood moves to Dunsinane Hill.

questions.q: Which character ultimately kills Macbeth in the final battle?
questions.explain: Macduff, who was "from his mother's womb untimely ripp'd", slays Macbeth and so fulfils the prophecy.

questions.q: In Jacobean England, the reigning monarch when Macbeth was written claimed descent from which character in the play?
questions.explain: James I traced his lineage to Banquo, which is why the witches show Banquo's descendants as future kings.

questions.q: In Macbeth, what do the three witches prophesy will happen to Macbeth at the start of the play?
options: He will be banished from Scotland
He will die in battle against Norway
He will become Thane of Cawdor and then king
He will father a line of kings
questions.explain: The witches hail Macbeth as Thane of Glamis, Thane of Cawdor, and one who shall be king hereafter.

questions.q: What does Lady Macbeth ask the spirits to do to her so she can help commit murder?
options: To give her the gift of prophecy
To protect her husband in battle
To "unsex" her and fill her with cruelty
questions.explain: She cries "unsex me here", asking to be stripped of feminine compassion to carry out the killing.

questions.q: The witches warn Macbeth to beware which character?
questions.explain: The first apparition warns Macbeth to "beware Macduff".

questions.q: After Duncan names his successor, who does Macbeth see as an obstacle to the throne?
questions.explain: Duncan declares Malcolm the Prince of Cumberland and heir, a step Macbeth must "o'erleap" to become king.

questions.q: Whose murder does Macbeth carry out to seize the throne?
questions.explain: Macbeth murders King Duncan in his sleep at Inverness to take the crown.

questions.q: What does Macbeth famously call life in his despairing speech after Lady Macbeth's death?
options: "A tale told by an idiot, full of sound and fury"
questions.explain: He calls life "a tale told by an idiot, full of sound and fury, signifying nothing", showing his nihilistic despair.

questions.q: Why does Macbeth have Banquo murdered after becoming king?
options: The witches prophesied Banquo's descendants would be kings
questions.explain: The witches foretold Banquo would father a line of kings, so Macbeth fears him and orders his death.

questions.q: What does the recurring imagery of blood most strongly symbolise in Macbeth?
options: Inescapable guilt and the consequences of murder
questions.explain: Blood that cannot be washed away, from Macbeth's hands to Lady Macbeth's "damned spot", represents unshakeable guilt.

questions.q: What prophecy gives Macbeth false confidence that no man can harm him?
options: That he will reign for forty years
That none of woman born shall harm him
That Banquo's heirs will spare him
That the witches will protect him
questions.explain: He believes "none of woman born" can kill him, until Macduff reveals he was born by Caesarean.

questions.q: Why is the theme of witchcraft especially significant in the Jacobean context of Macbeth?
options: Witchcraft was illegal to depict on stage
The Pope had recently endorsed witch-hunts
King James I was deeply interested in witchcraft and wrote a book, Daemonologie
Shakespeare himself was tried for witchcraft
questions.explain: James I wrote Daemonologie and believed in witches, so the supernatural would have unsettled his court.

questions.q: How does Lady Macbeth die?
options: She apparently takes her own life
questions.explain: Her death is reported and understood to be suicide, the consequence of overwhelming guilt.

questions.q: How is the prophecy about Birnam Wood ultimately fulfilled?
options: Malcolm's soldiers cut branches as camouflage as they advance
questions.explain: Malcolm's army cuts boughs from Birnam Wood to disguise their numbers, so the wood appears to move on Dunsinane.

questions.q: What does Macbeth hallucinate seeing before he murders Duncan?
options: A dagger leading him toward the chamber
questions.explain: He asks "Is this a dagger which I see before me?", a vision drawing him to commit the murder.

questions.q: How does Macduff's family meet its fate in the play?
options: Macbeth has them slaughtered at Macduff's castle
questions.explain: Macbeth orders the murder of Lady Macduff and her children at Fife after Macduff flees to England.

questions.q: Which contemporary event involving a plot against King James influences the play's themes of treason and regicide?
questions.explain: The 1605 Gunpowder Plot to kill James I made treason and regicide especially resonant for Jacobean audiences.

questions.q: What does Lady Macbeth famously do in her sleep later in the play, revealing her guilt?
options: She tries to wash imagined blood from her hands
questions.explain: In her sleepwalking scene she rubs her hands crying "Out, damned spot!", haunted by guilt over Duncan's blood.

questions.q: Whose ghost appears to Macbeth at the banquet, terrifying him in front of his guests?
questions.explain: Banquo, murdered on Macbeth's orders, returns as a ghost only Macbeth can see at the feast.
